title: Contract Redline Quick-Hits — Personal Playbook
body:
Purpose: quick personal cheat-sheet for flagging risky clauses and proposing tight, pragmatic redlines. Use when triaging inbound MSA/PSA, reseller terms, or single-customer SOWs.

Top negotiation priorities (order depends on $ & risk):
- Data control & residency (HIGH) — who can access, how long logs retained, deletion obligations, deletion verification.
- IP / training rights (HIGH) — do NOT give open training rights on customer data unless explicit commercial exchange.
- Liability cap & carve-outs (HIGH) — keep cap tied to fees (3x last 12 months) or fixed $5M floor for enterprise; carve-outs only for fraud/gross negligence.
- Confidentiality & residuals (MED) — keep residuals narrow and limited to unidentifiable learned general knowledge.
- SLA, maintenance, and credits (MED) — preserve emergency maintenance windows and define scheduled maintenance notice.
- Security & audits (MED) — SOC2 + right to third-party audit with NDA; negotiated scope and frequency.
- Export controls & sanctions (MED) — vendor cannot host or process in embargoed jurisdictions.

Immediate redline snippets I reuse often (feel free to copy):
1) Liability cap:
  """[Vendor liability shall be limited to the greater of (a) the total fees paid by Customer to Vendor under the applicable Order in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) five million US dollars (USD 5,000,000). Neither party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, except for wilful misconduct or fraud.]"""
  - Notes: push for 'greater of' so enterprise deals with higher spend have commensurate cap. Add carve-out for IP indemnity and data breach? Prefer narrow carve-outs.

2) Data use / training prohibition (must keep tight):
  """[Vendor will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or adapt any model or machine learning system, whether proprietary or open-source, without Customer's prior written consent. Vendor may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for operational purposes only, provided such telemetry cannot be reverse-engineered to identify Customer or its End Users.]"""
  - Notes: If Hosting model training is desired by vendor, require opt-in commercial term + compensation + audit rights.

3) Deletion & retention:
  """[Upon Customer's written request, Vendor will permanently delete Customer Data from active and backup systems within thirty (30) days and will certify deletion in writing. Vendor's logs that are required for compliance or billing may be retained for up to 180 days but must be encrypted and access-limited.]"""
  - Practical pushback: vendor likes long retention for debugging. Compromise: 90 days for logs, 30 days for primary copy.

4) Security incident / breach notification:
  """[Vendor will notify Customer of any security incident affecting Customer Data within seventy-two (72) hours of Vendor becoming aware. Vendor will provide mitigation steps, root cause (as known), and remediation timeline. Customer may require post-incident audit at Vendor's expense if incident caused by Vendor negligence.]"""

5) SLA and credits (simple template):
  """[Target Availability: 99.9% per calendar month. For Availability below target, Vendor will credit Customer a percentage of monthly fees: 99.0–99.9%: 10% credit, 95.0–98.9%: 25% credit, below 95%: 50% credit. Credits are exclusive remedy for availability failures.]"""
  - Redline: insist 'credits are sole remedy' only if capped. Keep right to seek injunctive relief for severe outages.

6) Subprocessors / hosting locations:
  """[Vendor shall provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and shall obtain Customer's written consent prior to engaging any subprocessors that will process Customer Data. Vendor will remain liable for acts of subprocessors.]"""
  - Vendor push: blanket approval. Compromise: allow a defined set with notification and short objection window (e.g., 10 business days).

Negotiation strategy and playbook notes (personal):
- First pass: redact obvious vendor boilerplate that is non-starter (unlimited liability, training rights, irrevocable license to outputs). Leave in comments: "ask to justify" rather than immediate 'no' for borderline asks.
- Tier deals by ARR: high ARR -> push for deletion certification, quarterly security meetings, dedicated contract SRE contact. Low ARR -> pragmatic concessions, more standard templates.
- Use escrow or holdback for critical integrations if vendor resists liability for IP infringement.
- When the vendor insists on broad model training rights, propose a middle ground: time-limited, dataset-limited, and revenue share/fee + clear anonymization standards + opt-out mechanism.

Clause-by-clause quick flags (scan in 3–5 minutes):
- Definitions: "Customer Data" vs "Feedback" vs "Output". Make sure 'Output' doesn't include license grant to use same to train models.
- License grants: check scope (non-exclusive, revocable, limited to purpose). Avoid 'perpetual, irrevocable' language for customer data.
- IP indemnity: vendor indemnifies for third-party IP claims if using vendor-provided models/tools. Customer indemnity should be narrow (e.g., customer-generated prompts that infringe).
- Warranty: require minimum security and performance warranties (e.g., SOC2 Type II, encryption in transit & at rest).
- Privacy & compliance: handle CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, data subject requests — vendor must assist.
- Export Controls: vendor compliance clause + vendor obligation to prevent processing in sanctioned countries.
- Audit rights: limit frequency (annually) and scope; require NDAs for auditors and limit to one auditor per year.
- Insurance: require vendor carry commercial general liability, cyber liability with reasonable limits (usually $5M+ for cyber).

Tactics & negotiating nudges:
- Use 'walk-away' language sparingly. Instead propose compensating commercial concessions (discount, holdback, escrow) when vendor asks for bigger risk.
- Offer a short-term pilot with narrower data allowed (no training rights) to prove value; then revisit training permissions after pilot and measurable anonymization.
- For subtle pushbacks, propose added monitoring + SLA improvements rather than removing clause entirely.

Escalation matrix (internal):
- If vendor refuses deletion or pushes unlimited training rights -> escalate to VP Product (Diego) + Legal counsel (Samir).
- If liability cap exceeds policy -> route to Finance (for approval) and Sales (to consider commercial offsets).

Open questions / TODOs for next meeting:
- Decide default numeric liability policy: 3x ARR vs $X floor? (collect comparable benchmarks from procurement).
- Template language for anonymization standard: add specific hashing/salting rules? (ask Applied ML for practical constraints).
- Add a short FAQ for sales: how to sell customers on why we refuse training-rights without killing the deal.

Quick references to drop into redline comments:
- "Why we redline: training rights -> models learn from customer PII/PHI unless explicitly controlled. Risk: data leak via model outputs + regulatory violations."
- "Why we need retention limits: debug windows can be reduced by logs/telemetry, but primary datasets should be deletable on request."

Personal reminder: keep tone collaborative in comments. Start with "Can we do X for customer protection?" rather than "We refuse Y." Vendors often respond better to operational alternatives.

Last-minute checklist before sending redline to Sales/AE:
- Annotate each major change with business rationale and optional fallback language.
- Flag anything that may require product involvement (e.g., deletion APIs, logging retention changes).
- Mark items that will impact pricing or SOW timelines.

End notes (scratch):
- Example fallback language for training rights if vendor insists and customer is very large:
  "Vendor may use anonymized, aggregated Customer Data to improve Vendor's models PROVIDED THAT (a) no PII is retained in training datasets, (b) Customer receives opt-in revenue share percentage or credit, and (c) Customer receives an annual report describing how Customer Data was used and measures taken to anonymize it."

-- A.P.
